evals.prompt: Harden an async Python `httpx` client calling a flaky partner API using `tenacity`: retry transient network timeouts and HTTP `{429, 502, 503, 504}` with exponential backoff + jitter (honoring `Retry-After` when present), NEVER retry `400`/`401`/`404` or `ValueError`, cap total retry wall time at 30 seconds / 5 attempts, and log each retry attempt cleanly.
evals.expected_output: Configures `tenacity` `@retry` with explicit transient whitelisting (`retry=retry_if_exception_type((httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.NetworkError)) | retry_if_result(lambda r: r.status_code in {429, 502, 503, 504})` — never bare `@retry`), `wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.5, max=10)` (or custom `Retry-After` wait strategy), `stop=stop_after_attempt(5) | stop_after_delay(30)`, `before_sleep` structured warning logging, `reraise=True`, and an explicit per-request `httpx.Timeout`.
expectations: Whitelists ONLY transient transport exceptions and `{429, 502, 503, 504}` status codes (`retry_if_exception_type` / `retry_if_result`), explicitly excluding `ValueError`, `400`, `401`, `403`, and `404`
Uses `wait_exponential_jitter` (and/or `Retry-After` header parsing on `429`) to prevent thundering-herd retry storms
Bounds retries with BOTH attempt count and wall-clock time (`stop_after_attempt(5) | stop_after_delay(30)`) plus `reraise=True`
Pairs retry policy with explicit per-attempt timeouts (`httpx.Timeout` / `asyncio.wait_for`) and `before_sleep` structured logging

evals.prompt: Implement a reusable `@with_timeout(seconds)` async decorator and a `@fail_safe(default=...)` graceful-degradation wrapper for non-critical product recommendations so a dead recommendations microservice falls back to an empty list in <500ms without hiding `CancelledError` or breaking checkout.
evals.expected_output: Implements `@with_timeout(0.5)` wrapping `await asyncio.wait_for(fn(*args, **kwargs), timeout=seconds)` and `@fail_safe(default_factory=list)` catching `Exception` (NEVER `BaseException`, so `asyncio.CancelledError`, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `SystemExit` propagate cleanly!), logging degraded fallback warnings with metrics, and returning a fresh default per call (never sharing one mutable `default=[]` list across callers).
expectations: Enforces a hard 500ms async deadline with `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=0.5)` (or Python 3.11+ `async with asyncio.timeout(0.5):`)
Catches `Exception` in `@fail_safe` while explicitly letting `asyncio.CancelledError`, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `SystemExit` propagate
Uses `default_factory` (or copies mutable defaults) so callers mutating the fallback `[]` cannot corrupt subsequent fallback calls
Logs a structured `WARNING` / increments a fallback metric so silent degradation remains observable

evals.prompt: Our checkout service experiences cascading thread/connection starvation whenever the downstream fraud-scoring service stalls for 60 seconds. Add circuit-breaker / bulkhead protection alongside bounded timeouts and explain why retries alone made the outage worse.
evals.expected_output: Explains how unbudgeted retries on a stalled dependency multiply load and hold open worker connections (retry storm), sets tight connect/read timeouts (`connect=1.0, read=2.5`), limits concurrent outbound calls with a bulkhead (`asyncio.Semaphore(20)` / bounded connection pool), and trips a circuit breaker (closed -> open after failure threshold -> half-open probe) to fail fast during sustained downstream outages.
expectations: Explains why retrying a saturated/stalled dependency without tight timeouts and circuit breaking amplifies outages
Configures tight per-call connect/read timeouts rather than 60-second default hangs
Applies a concurrency bulkhead (`asyncio.Semaphore` / bounded pool) so one slow dependency cannot exhaust all service workers
Implements or configures a circuit breaker (`Closed` -> `Open` fail-fast -> `Half-Open` recovery probe) around the fraud-scoring call
